title: Completion of an injective finite algebra with DVR branches
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], where local means that $\mathfrak m$ is the unique maximal ideal. Let $A\hookrightarrow B$ be an injective homomorphism of commutative rings making $B$ a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Assume that $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ contracting to $\mathfrak m$, where localization at primes is as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Put $R=\widehat A=\varprojlim_n A/\mathfrak m^n$ and $C=B\otimes_A R$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-module-base-change]. Then the set of primes $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak m$ is finite and there is a canonical isomorphism $$C\cong\prod_{\mathfrak q\mid\mathfrak m}\widehat{B_{\mathfrak q}}$$ compatible with both the $B$- and $R$-algebra structures. Each factor is a discrete valuation ring, hence a normal domain, meaning a domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. The map $A\to R$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and the structural map $i:R\to C$, $r\mapsto1\otimes r$, is injective. Both $R$ and $C$ are reduced (they have no nonzero nilpotent elements); $R$ is Noetherian local of dimension $1$; and $C$ is a finite $R$-module, integral over $R$, and Noetherian. Finally $C$ is integrally closed in $Q(C)$, where $Q(C)$ is its localization at all non-zero-divisors (elements $s$ such that $sx=0$ implies $x=0$).

source.place: Tag 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion), final paragraph: product of completed local DVRs. Agent-explicit finite-algebra formulation, also recording flat injection and normality before any birational comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] to the finite map $A\to B$ at $\mathfrak m$. Since every element outside $\mathfrak m$ is a unit, $A_{\mathfrak m}=A$ by $a/s\mapsto as^{-1}$. The cited statement gives finiteness of the primes over $\mathfrak m$ and an isomorphism $R\otimes_A B\cong\prod_{\mathfrak q\mid\mathfrak m}D_{\mathfrak q}$, where $D_{\mathfrak q}=\widehat{B_{\mathfrak q}}$, compatible with $B$ and $R$. Precompose with tensor symmetry $b\otimes r\mapsto r\otimes b$. In particular $b\otimes r$ maps in coordinate $\mathfrak q$ to the product of the completion image of $b$ and the image of $r$ under the completed local map $R\to D_{\mathfrak q}$; this gives exactly both algebra compatibilities in the statement.

source.place: Tag 07N9, lemma-completion-finite-extension; specialize at the maximal ideal

proof.text: For every indexing prime, $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a DVR by hypothesis. Its Noetherian local-domain and nonzero principal-maximal-ideal characterization is included in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-completion-of-dvr-is-dvr] applies and gives that $D_{\mathfrak q}$ is a DVR. Each $D_{\mathfrak q}$ is therefore a principal ideal domain by that definition, and [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] makes it a normal domain, in particular integrally closed in its fraction field.

source.place: Tag 0AP1, lemma-completion-dvr; Algebra Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr) and Tag 00GZ (lemma-PID-normal)

proof.text: The map $A\to R$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat]. The definition [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] thus sends the injective $A$-linear map $A\hookrightarrow B$ to an injection $A\otimes_A R\to B\otimes_A R$. Under $A\otimes_A R\cong R$, $a\otimes r\mapsto ar$ with inverse $r\mapsto1\otimes r$, this injection is $i(r)=1\otimes r$. This proves injectivity of $i$.

If $c^n=0$ in $C$, every coordinate of its image under step 1 is nilpotent in the domain $D_{\mathfrak q}$, hence zero, so $c=0$. Thus $C$ is reduced. If $r^n=0$ in $R$, then $i(r)^n=0$, so $i(r)=0$ and injectivity from step 3 implies $r=0$. Thus $R$ is reduced as well.

source.place: Tag 0C3V, lemma-normalization-same-after-completion, final paragraph; elementary reducedness consequence of the displayed product

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $R$ is Noetherian local. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension], $\dim R=\dim A=1$. Choose finite $A$-module generators $b_1,\ldots,b_t$ of $B$. The elements $b_j\otimes1$ generate $C$ over $R$: if $b=\sum_j a_jb_j$ then $b\otimes r=\sum_j (b_j\otimes1)(a_jr)$, and every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors. Therefore $C$ is finite over $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] to $R\to C$ to obtain integrality and Noetherianity.

Use the product in step 1 to write $C=\prod D_{\mathfrak q}$. Let $x=c/s\in Q(C)$ be integral over $C$, so $s$ is a non-zero-divisor. Every coordinate $s_{\mathfrak q}$ is nonzero: otherwise $s$ annihilates the nonzero tuple supported at $\mathfrak q$ with coordinate $1$. The coordinate fraction $c_{\mathfrak q}/s_{\mathfrak q}$ satisfies the projected monic equation for $x$, and hence belongs to $D_{\mathfrak q}$ by step 2. Write it as $d_{\mathfrak q}$ and let $d=(d_{\mathfrak q})\in C$. Coordinatewise $c=sd$, so $x=d/1$ by the fraction relation [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Thus every element integral over $C$ lies in $C$, precisely integral closedness [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].
